page: Amazon Web Services c8in.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 3.9 GHz, providing 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network infrastructure is a key attribute of the c8in.16xlarge, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. The instance contains zero hardware GPUs and does not bundle local storage, requiring network-attached block storage options such as Amazon EBS for persistent data holding. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high core density and fast clock speeds against a modest memory footprint. This makes it cost-efficient for workloads that demand significant raw processing speed and high network throughput without consuming large amounts of RAM per core. Primary workloads include distributed high-performance computing, network-intensive batch processing, video encoding, media transcoding, and scalable web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. It offers 64 vCPUs mapped across 32 dedicated physical cores and is configured with 128.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. The instance features a 100 Gbps baseline network throughput, providing substantial capacity for data transfer. It does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures. Given its combination of strong clock performance, high vCPU capacity, and large network bandwidth, c8in.16xlarge provides high resource efficiency for compute-intensive and network-bound applications such as distributed analytics, video rendering, scientific simulation pipelines, and high-throughput application servers.
